title: Climate refugee resettlement: rights protection and cultural gain and loss

context_sources.name: Norman Myers, Environmental Refugees in a Globally Warmed World, 1993
Davis and Caldeira, Consumption-based accounting of CO2 emissions, 2010

limitations: Watermark glyphs break lines and merge into words throughout.
The notation table is misaligned, so several symbols are defined twice with different meanings.
The swing-culture formula is garbled by line-break artifacts.
The two refugee-count ranges in one section disagree.

tasks: Count people displaced by sea-level rise in six states
Rank the drivers of cultural loss
Match each displaced population to a receiving country
Track human-rights protection as arrivals dilute resources
Split culture into gain, loss and a switch, and time the balance
Turn policy into parameter changes and revise the model

section_map.summary: Five tasks: count, match, simulate rights and culture, set policy, revise.
Island states at risk, IPCC's 150 million by 2050, cooperation still thin.
Nine assumptions, from the five-meter rule to perfect compliance.
Regression for six states and a six-factor cultural-loss index.
Three-factor fit, weights 0.57, 0.34, 0.08, assignment by matching.
Rights diluted by arrival; culture split into gain, loss and switch.
Resettlement, education, jobs and cultural policy, read as parameter changes.
Births and deaths added; policy called effective though idealized.
Four strengths, four weaknesses, four extensions.
Myers, Davis and Caldeira, Tylor, and the UN ruling.

contributions.summary: Duty measured by consumer-based emissions over distance, so traded emissions still count.
Culture classed by the sign of its economic effect, with lifestyle flipping at a tolerance threshold.
The rights index revised twice, once for policy and once for births and deaths.

dependency_graph.handoff: The populations counted as displaced are the groups the assignment then places
The loss-risk factors motivate splitting culture by the sign of its effect
The chosen destination is the country whose per-person resources the arrivals then dilute
The culture balance and the rights index are the two tests the policy is judged against

assumptions.summary: Below five meters, residents must move.
Whole populations move together, and destinations may refuse when full.
Policy is carried out exactly, so it can be read as a parameter change.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Six-country table of population, low-lying land share, terrain height and annual rise.
Education levels, GDP per head, past migration outcomes, distance and consumer emissions.

models.summary: Regression of sea-level rise against landform, with a five-meter cutoff.
Six-factor cultural-loss index from principal components.
Weighted three-factor fit solved as an assignment problem.
Five-indicator rights index diluted by arrivals and repaired by policy.
Three-type culture model with a tolerance switch.

verification.summary: No-policy simulation shows the rights index falling as arrivals grow.
Adding births and deaths is judged closer to reality by eye.

results_trace.summary: 200 to 300 thousand displaced by 2080, restated as 300 to 400 thousand.
Weights 0.57, 0.34, 0.08, and one worked fit of 2.0416.
Diverse hosts rebalance without policy; single-group hosts show net cultural loss.

writing_logic.summary: Consumer-based emissions chosen over producer-based because trade moves emissions.
Conflict from belief declared unavoidable before any remedy is offered.
The model is corrected because its own results contradicted its assumptions.

language_observations.summary: Benefit and harm assigned to different countries, so both stand.
An algebra change narrated as denominator up, share down, anger follows.
A chain of escalation from difference to war, each step one degree worse.
The forecast marked as too low in the same breath as it is given.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1: bipartite graph, origins on the left and destinations on the right.
Figure 2: the protection index falling over time with no policy.
Figure 3: the index recovering once policy adds resources and employment.
Figure 4: the index after births and deaths enter, judged more realistic.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Measuring obligation by consumption rather than production anticipates the fairness objection.
Aiming protection at the weaker culture, and at its aging bearers, is more concrete than a general appeal.
Calling the policy idealized while still defending its direction reads as judgment rather than advocacy.

weaknesses.summary: One section gives two inconsistent ranges for the same forecast.
The cultural-loss index is never evaluated for any country.
The assignment model never produces an assignment.
The model promises the date of cultural balance and never gives one.

independent_extensions.summary: Reconcile the two refugee ranges and publish the regression.
Run the assignment and name the destinations.
Choose among storm, submergence and salinization as the trigger.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: When trade moves the burden, measure it where it is consumed.
Give each group its own resettlement form and say who it suits.

unresolved_questions.question: Which forecast stands, 200 to 300 thousand or 300 to 400 thousand?
Which destination does the matching assign to each state?
When does the cultural gain-loss balance return?
